chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Hashim, from Anbasa al-Abid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah loves the servant that he seeks (forgiveness) to Him regarding the grievous crime, and He hates the servant if he takes lightly with the small crime.

key_terms.يَسْتَخِفَّ: To take lightly, to trivialize, or to be complacent

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in how Allah views repentance for major sins versus minor sins?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni uses this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to refine the concept of *tawbah* (repentance), emphasizing that the sincerity of repentance is measured by the gravity with which one acknowledges the sin. This teaching warns against *istikhfaf* (trivialization), a spiritual danger where minor sins accumulate due to a lack of reverence, while major sins require profound humility to ensure the repentance is accepted. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the internal state of the heart during repentance is as critical as the act itself.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abdul Rahman Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Hashim, from Anbasa Al Aabid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Loves the servant that he seeks (Forgiveness) to Him<sup>azwj</sup> regarding the grievous crime and He<sup>azwj</sup> Hates the servant if he takes lightly with the small crime’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Ali from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn abu Hashim from ‘Anbasah al-‘Abid from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Allah loves that a servant asks Him for help in great crimes and He hates the servant who considers trivial sins insignificant.’”
